subject: medicine
title: Pituitary adenomas, acromegaly and Sheehan's syndrome

steps.tx: Take a focused history for suspected pituitary disease. Ask about **acromegaly** features such as enlarging rings and shoes, jaw growth, headache, sweating and oily skin. Ask about **galactorrhoea** with amenorrhoea, infertility and low libido. Ask about weight gain with striae and high sugar, postpartum bleeding with absent milk in **Sheehan syndrome**, visual bumps while driving and new thirst with frequent night urination.
steps.say: When you take the history, ask about slow changes in the face, hands, rings and shoes over many years. Ask about milky nipple discharge, missed periods, infertility and reduced interest in close relationships. Ask about weight gain with stretch marks, raised pressure and sugar, and about heavy bleeding after delivery followed by absent milk. Also ask about bumping into objects at the sides, new thirst and passing large volumes of urine at night.

vis.alt: Three side-by-side images: a normal face, an acromegalic patient with prominent jaw and brow, and a pale woman representing Sheehan's syndrome.
vis.caption: Characteristic facial and physical profiles of acromegaly and Sheehan's syndrome

steps.tx: Examine the hands for spade shaped enlargement with sweaty doughy grip, then study the face for **prognathism** with prominent brow, widely spaced teeth and enlarged tongue. Look for oily skin with tags, acne and excess hair, test visual fields for **bitemporal hemianopia** by confrontation and check for expressible milk. Note pallor with absent axillary hair in **Sheehan syndrome**, raised pressure in cortisol excess and tall stature in gigantism.
steps.say: Start with the hands and look for broad spade shaped enlargement with a sweaty doughy handshake. Study the face for a protruding jaw, heavy brow, gaps between the teeth and a large tongue. Inspect the skin for oiliness, tags, acne and extra hair, then test the visual fields at the bedside for loss on both outer sides. Check for expressible milky discharge, record the pressure and height, and note pallor with absent underarm hair after an obstetric bleed.

steps.tx: Confirm excess or deficiency with targeted blood tests. Measure **IGF-1** with growth hormone suppression on glucose load to confirm acromegaly, check prolactin for adenoma or stalk effect, screen cortisol for ACTH excess and test thyroid and gonadal axes for central deficiency. Request **MRI pituitary** to show the adenoma, stalk and chiasm, chart Goldmann fields for bitemporal loss and use water deprivation testing when diabetes insipidus is suspected.
steps.say: Confirm the clinical suspicion with blood tests that measure growth hormone action, prolactin, cortisol and thyroid and gonadal axes. An unsuppressed growth hormone level after a glucose load confirms acromegaly, while a very high prolactin points toward a large prolactinoma. Request magnetic resonance imaging of the pituitary to show the adenoma and its relation to the stalk and chiasm. Chart the visual fields formally and test thirst and urine concentration when diabetes insipidus is suspected.

steps.tx: Study this coronal magnetic resonance image of the pituitary. A large **macroadenoma** fills and expands the sella with mixed signal tissue. The **optic chiasm** above it is stretched, compressed and pushed upward by the mass. This picture explains bitemporal field loss in such patients and reminds you to request **MRI pituitary** with formal field charting whenever chiasmal compression is suspected.
steps.say: Look at this coronal magnetic resonance image and find the large pituitary mass filling the sella. Notice how the optic chiasm above the gland is stretched and pushed upward by the tumour. This compression explains why these patients lose vision on both outer sides. Whenever you suspect this pattern, request magnetic resonance imaging of the pituitary and chart the visual fields formally without delay.

vis.alt: Coronal brain MRI showing large pituitary macroadenoma with compressed and elevated optic chiasm above it.
vis.caption: Coronal MRI shows pituitary macroadenoma compressing and elevating optic chiasm. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Remove suitable adenomas by **transsphenoidal surgery** and control residual growth hormone excess with octreotide or pegvisomant after surgery or radiotherapy. Shrink prolactinomas with **cabergoline** as first therapy. Replace **Sheehan syndrome** deficiency with hydrocortisone first, add levothyroxine only after cortisol cover, then sex steroids, with desmopressin spray for diabetes insipidus. Watch for apoplexy with sudden headache, cerebrospinal fluid leak and the danger of thyroxine before steroids.
steps.say: Treat suitable adenomas by arranging surgical removal through the nose and sphenoid sinus. Control remaining growth hormone excess with somatostatin analogues or growth hormone receptor blockade, and shrink prolactinomas with dopamine agonist tablets. Replace cortisol before thyroid hormone in Sheehan syndrome, then add thyroid hormone and sex steroids, and control water loss with desmopressin spray. Monitor the insulin like growth factor level, prolactin and repeat imaging, and act urgently for sudden headache that suggests apoplexy.
